t: This morning, the ground let go of me.
Nobody takes off their boots in Gusthollow.
Whoever does, the wind carries them over the mountains.
I took mine off.
The wind here never stops. It has blown the same way for three hundred years.
Our trees grow sideways. Our smoke goes sideways.
Our laundry has never once hung down.
Every house is chained to the ground. Four chains each.
Our boots are iron. Ten pounds each.
Babies get their first pair before their first word.
At weddings, we tie the bride to the groom, so nobody blows away from the altar.
We all walk leaning forward, like we're climbing a hill that isn't there.
Old Marta sells soup. In cups with lids.
On the tower, we painted three words. Boots on. Always.
My little sister Pip is seven. She's the lightest kid in town.
She has rocks sewn into her pockets. She still wobbles.
And she loves kites. The wind has taken every kite she ever had.
One day, she says, I'm going to see where they go.
Fifty years ago, a boy named Tobb took off his boots to dry his feet.
Just for one second.
The wind picked him up like a leaf.
We watched him go over the mountains, still holding one sock.
He walked back home. It took him three years.
He said the other side was green. Nobody believed him.
Now he's old Tobb, and his boots are the heaviest in town.
This morning, the wind doubled.
Chains snapped. The bakery roof flew off like a hat.
And Pip was up on the hill, with a brand new kite.
The string pulled. Her boot strap broke.
One boot came off. Then the other.
And my sister went up.
She grabbed the weathervane on top of the tower, and held on.
Nobody could climb up. The wind pushed us flat on the ground.
And the weathervane started to bend.
There was only one way to get up there.
I sat down. I untied my laces.
Old Tobb grabbed my arm. Don't, he said.
I pulled off my left boot. Then my right.
And the ground let go of me.
I flew. Faster than the bakery roof.
I hit the tower. I grabbed the vane. I grabbed Pip.
The vane broke off.
And we both went over the mountains.
I held her as tight as I could.
Below us, rocks. Then snow. Then clouds.
And then, green.
A valley with no wind at all.
Trees growing straight up. Smoke going straight up.
And kites. Hundreds of kites, lying in the grass.
Every kite Pip ever lost.
We landed on our backs in the soft grass.
Told you, Pip said. I wanted to see where they go.
Tobb was right all along.
My whole life, I kept my boots on.
Tomorrow, I'm walking home, to tell everyone to take them off.
